content.thinking: I notice the ClientDisconnected errors actually start at 17:31, slightly before the claimed onset, so I should flag that as a caveat rather than an exact match. The rollback mitigation and recovery support the root cause, but since it wasn't independently verified by a code diff, I'll note that as an assumption alongside the 0.85 confidence level before writing up the fields.

assumptions: The deploy was identified as the cause by correlation (it landed in the same minute as the latency jump) plus the fact that rolling it back restored baseline; the specific O(n^2) change in average_spend_per_item was inferred from the change event and not independently verified against the diff or a profile during the incident.

The logs show account-page ClientDisconnected errors and 0.5-1.5% per-minute error rates already running from 17:31, before the 17:37 deploy. These were treated as pre-existing background noise consistent with the stated baseline error rate, but that was assumed rather than investigated; if they are related, the onset may be earlier than 17:37.
Impact is assumed to fall mainly on shoppers with substantial purchase history, since the cost of the change scales with the number of prior purchases. Per-customer impact was not measured.
Recovery is taken from the metrics returning to baseline at 17:43 and a single post-rollback check; no extended soak was performed to confirm the fix held.
The flag provider showed no recent flag changes, so configuration changes were ruled out; no other services were examined for related impact.
input.executive_summary: For roughly six minutes on 26 September 2026 (17:37-17:43 UTC), the account page on the shop service became very slow. Customers viewing their account — particularly those with a longer purchase history — saw pages take seconds instead of being near-instant, and a small share gave up or timed out before the page loaded. Over that window a modestly larger fraction of requests failed than normally would; failures were concentrated on the account page, and no orders or customer data were lost. The cause was a code change released that afternoon that made an account-page calculation far more expensive than it needed to be. Automated response detected the problem, identified the release as the likely cause, and reverted it; the service returned to normal behaviour within about a minute of the action, and a draft pull request has been opened to correct the calculation before it is re-released.
input.root_cause: A deploy of io-shop that landed at 17:37 changed `average_spend_per_item` to recompute a running sum over all prior purchases for each purchase in the list — an O(n²) loop — rather than reusing the already-computed total, which made account-page rendering CPU-bound and slow for any shopper with real purchase history (p50 ~45ms → 277-460ms, p95/p99 ~210/380ms → 2000-3800ms at the 17:37 bucket), causing shoppers to time out or abandon (ClientDisconnected). Rolling the deploy back returned the service to baseline, which confirms the deploy as the cause.
